name: Linocut Masjid
summary: A chunky, hand-carved mosque pairs irregular black architecture with an acid-olive minaret on warm paper.
why: Broad angular edges and deliberate chisel-like changes make the mosque feel cut from a printing block. Its dome, substantial square minaret, and one large doorway stay legible without tiny texture. The offbeat olive second ink adds a contemporary printmaking character.
risk: The rough edges deliberately sacrifice architectural precision. The printmaking style can feel more expressive and artisanal than polished or formal.
sub1: Bold edges with a handmade rhythm
reasonToChoose: You want a mosque with the character of a handmade print.

palette.name: LINOCUT / WARM PAPER + CARBON + ACID OLIVE
